title: A Group Chat for the Yearbook
premise: Theo Sandoval, the overlooked statistician of Westfield High's championship basketball team, has quietly documented that the star players' grades are being falsified to keep them eligible. When he finds coded instructions hidden in his late grandmother's recipe box, he discovers she ran an anonymous student whistleblower network decades ago — and the codes are a map to her old dead-drop system, still functional. Theo revives the network under the handle 'Recipe Box,' exposing the grade-rigging scheme run by Coach Brandt and Principal Okafor, but as his anonymous power grows, he starts manipulating classmates for 'the greater good,' becoming what he fought. In the climax, the administration traces the account and threatens expulsion; Theo must choose between protecting himself by burning an innocent scapegoat or going public with everything, including his own abuses. He confesses all — the coach falls, Theo accepts suspension, and he rebuilds the network as an open, accountable student press collective rather than a secret weapon.
about_author: Juniper Delacroix is a former high school newspaper adviser who spent six years watching teenagers discover how institutions really work. She writes from a converted garden shed in coastal Oregon, where she keeps her own grandmother's recipe box on the desk for luck.

chapters.title: Boxed Instructions
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Theo's POV. While clearing out his grandmother's house, Theo finds a recipe card reading 'Sift twice. Serve cold. Deliver to locker 214.' Curiosity beats grief; he checks the abandoned locker and finds a rusted drop box with decades-old notes. Emotional beat: loneliness meeting the first hint that someone like him once mattered.

chapters.title: The Rigged Box Score
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Back at school, Theo cross-checks game eligibility forms against transcript data and confirms three starters have impossible grades. He says nothing — he's learned that being right gets statisticians benched socially. Beat: quiet resentment hardening into resolve as he pockets the evidence instead of reporting it.

chapters.title: Serve Cold
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following the recipe cards' cipher, Theo posts his first anonymous exposé on a resurrected blog: 'The Grade Factory.' The school erupts; his best friend Priya defends the accused players fiercely, unknowingly arguing with Theo online. Beat: intoxicating thrill of invisible power — and the first lie told to a friend.

chapters.title: Locker 214 Replies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Marisol, a junior journalist who finds a note in the drop box responding to 'Recipe Box' — someone else knows the old system exists. She becomes Theo's unwitting correspondent while suspecting her lab partner. Beat: connection through secrecy; two lonely people building trust on false foundations.

chapters.title: What the Network Owes You
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Emboldened, Theo leaks a second story targeting a popular teacher over a minor infraction to test his reach — and destroys a career for no real reason. Priya notices the blog's cruelty shifting. Beat: corruption of motive; power feels like justice until it doesn't.

chapters.title: Marisol's Hunch
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol matches the blog's posting times to Theo's library computer logins and confronts him gently. He denies it, then recruits her anyway, half-confessing. Together they plan the big reveal on Brandt and Okafor. Beat: intimacy built on complicity; the reader sees Theo sliding further than he admits.

chapters.title: Counterplay
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The administration hires a tech forensics firm; a trap post lures the account into revealing metadata. Theo realizes they're closing in and considers framing a scapegoat — a slacker classmate with a grudge history. Beat: moral nadir; he drafts the frame-up and can't delete it.

chapters.title: The Scapegoat Draft
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol discovers the draft framing their classmate and gives Theo an ultimatum: burn it or lose her. Grandma's final recipe card surfaces — 'A cook who poisons the meal owns the poison.' Beat: confrontation as mirror; Theo finally sees the administrator in himself.

chapters.title: Everything, Signed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Traced and summoned before the school board, Theo publishes the full archive — the grade fraud AND his own manipulations — under his real name at the meeting. Chaos; Brandt resigns mid-hearing; Theo accepts suspension. Beat: climax as self-indictment; justice that includes himself.

chapters.title: Open Kitchen
chapters.summary: Epilogue-ish, alternating Theo and Marisol POV. Serving his suspension, Theo co-founds an open-byline student press collective with Marisol — no anonymity, no secrets, editors and corrections pages. Locker 214 becomes a public suggestion box. Beat: belonging earned honestly; power shared instead of hoarded.
